correctness.rationale: The preorder-polytope inequality system for two antichains is derived exactly. For each lower point x, the upper slice equals a unit cube plus (m-sum x) times the coordinate simplex, giving a finite convex generator set with lower coordinates binary. Strict convexity reduces any diameter pair to two generators. Direct inequalities bound distinct-peak pairs by 2(m+1)^2+n-2, with strict slack (m-k)(m+k+1)+(m-k_prime)(m+k_prime+1), and bound same/absent-peak pairs strictly below. Equality enforces zero lower blocks, distinct full-height upper peaks and complementary binary other coordinates, proving count choose(n,2)*2^(n-2). Standalone Python reproduces 4,983,576 exact-integer assertions; finite ranges do not substitute for proof.

value.rationale: The two-antichain preorder polytope is a natural recently introduced infinite two-parameter family studied for lattice enumerators, with no known exact Euclidean diameter classification. The theorem yields a closed metric invariant and exhaustive extremal-vertex pair structure with an exponential pair count independent of m, even as the diameter scales with m. Its cube-plus-variable-simplex representation explains a robust geometric rigidity beyond a one-off computation; this is a motivated complete classification, not an arbitrary slice or minor numerical improvement.
